sources.vendor_claim: The official product page presents an office-oriented AI Agent workspace with task orchestration, office-tool connections, and result delivery.
sources.current_model_signal: The platform may expose selectable models; this register does not treat one foundation model as a verified fixed WorkBuddy capability.
sources.anti_fomo_comparison: Anti-FOMO has stronger evidence-bound decision and acceptance records, while WorkBuddy emphasizes broader office execution and delivery.
sources.next_step: Retain a controlled, allowlisted external-result return boundary with provenance and fail-closed review.
sources.risk: A vendor product claim does not prove official account integration or authorize task execution.

sources.vendor_claim: Official documentation presents an AI-native development environment that uses repository context to assist engineering work.
sources.current_model_signal: TRAE model availability is product- and account-dependent; no single model is promoted into this register without stable official evidence.
sources.anti_fomo_comparison: TRAE is stronger for coding execution; Anti-FOMO is intentionally focused on evidence-led research and decision delivery.
sources.next_step: Keep scoped context and verification patterns without adding autonomous code, terminal, or repository writes.
sources.risk: AI IDE execution would materially expand the product and permission boundary.

sources.vendor_claim: The official introduction presents a natural-language office platform for documents, data, and editable deliverables with DingTalk ecosystem integration.
sources.current_model_signal: The office product and selectable Qwen foundation models are tracked separately; capability equivalence is not inferred from model branding.
sources.anti_fomo_comparison: QwenWork emphasizes low-friction Office creation; Anti-FOMO has stronger source lineage and acceptance gates but weaker real Office evidence.
sources.next_step: Build editable artifact lineage and real Office/visual receipts without claiming a QwenWork or DingTalk connector.
sources.risk: Generated files and ecosystem access require explicit data permissions and attributable acceptance.

sources.vendor_claim: The official page emphasizes a context workspace that aligns intent, tool chains, plans, validation, and rollback.
sources.current_model_signal: LangHub is evaluated as a context and workflow product; no fixed underlying model is asserted by this register.
sources.anti_fomo_comparison: LangHub has a broader context-workspace proposition; Anti-FOMO has more explicit evidence and release-state separation.
sources.next_step: Build consented project context, retention, change preview, and project-scoped undo.
sources.risk: Silent cross-project memory would undermine consent and provenance.

sources.vendor_claim: Official documentation presents a desktop office agent for local file, data, and office-automation tasks.
sources.current_model_signal: Baidu foundation-model candidates are tracked separately from the DuMate desktop-control product claim.
sources.anti_fomo_comparison: DuMate emphasizes desktop execution; Anti-FOMO intentionally keeps file and desktop actions outside the current authorization boundary.
sources.next_step: Require sandbox, minimum permissions, audit, dry-run, and rollback design before any desktop-agent reconsideration.
sources.risk: Desktop control and arbitrary local-file writes are high-impact actions.

sources.vendor_claim: Official documentation presents a local AI Agent based on the OpenClaw ecosystem that can receive office, creative, and development tasks through messaging entry points.
sources.current_model_signal: QClaw model selection is configuration-dependent; no fixed foundation model is asserted here.
sources.anti_fomo_comparison: QClaw emphasizes remote local-device execution; Anti-FOMO is stronger in reviewable evidence but intentionally excludes message-triggered device control.
sources.next_step: Keep messaging inputs from directly authorizing device actions; preserve explicit proposals and human approvals only.
sources.risk: Remote message-triggered device execution creates privilege and prompt-injection risk.

sources.vendor_claim: Codex is presented as a coding agent for parallel engineering workflows, code changes, tests, reviews, and scheduled background work.
sources.current_model_signal: GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna for current general workflows; GPT-5.3-Codex for specialized agentic coding.
sources.anti_fomo_comparison: Anti-FOMO has a stronger source-to-decision evidence boundary, but does not provide a general coding or terminal agent.
sources.next_step: Retain scoped context, diff, verification, and handoff patterns without adding autonomous code execution.
sources.risk: Repository or terminal actions would materially expand Anti-FOMO permissions.

sources.vendor_claim: Claude Code is presented as a terminal-based coding agent with project context and enterprise deployment options.
sources.current_model_signal: Claude Opus 5 is the official strongest Claude Pro model signal observed on 2026-08-31.
sources.anti_fomo_comparison: Anti-FOMO provides reviewable evidence and action proposals but intentionally lacks arbitrary terminal or code write access.
sources.next_step: Keep local permissions, identity, audit, dry-run, and rollback as hard prerequisites for any future tool integration.
sources.risk: Unbounded local execution and file write access conflict with the current product boundary.

sources.source_title: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform agents overview
sources.vendor_claim: Google documents agent identity, tool registries, policy governance, evaluation, observability, and managed agent runtime capabilities.
sources.current_model_signal: Gemini 3.7 Flash is positioned for complex agentic tasks at scale; Gemini 3.1 Pro remains the complex-task Pro model in the official model list.
sources.anti_fomo_comparison: Anti-FOMO is more focused on evidence-bound Chinese decision workflows; its agent lifecycle inventory and operational observability are less broad.
sources.next_step: Build a signed skill inventory, permission preview, offline evaluation, and read-only release linkage.
sources.risk: A broad platform build would dilute Anti-FOMO's decision-evidence differentiation.

sources.vendor_claim: Microsoft documents agent creation, testing, evaluation, publishing, monitoring, connector governance, and audit controls.
sources.current_model_signal: The platform is model-configurable; no single foundation model is treated as the product capability in this register.
sources.anti_fomo_comparison: Anti-FOMO is narrower and locally evidence-led; Copilot Studio has a stronger enterprise connector and lifecycle-control surface.
sources.next_step: Use version-level acceptance packets, tool permission previews, human approval, and audit handoff rather than copying a connector marketplace.
sources.risk: Connector breadth creates identity, data movement, and publication risk.

sources.vendor_claim: The official repository describes an LLM application framework using instruction following, tools, planning, and memory, with browser and code-interpreter examples.
sources.current_model_signal: The official Qwen-Agent repository recorded Qwen3.5 agent examples in February 2026.
sources.anti_fomo_comparison: Anti-FOMO has stronger evidence and release boundaries, while Qwen-Agent offers a more flexible model and tool framework.
sources.next_step: Evaluate model-agnostic tool protocols while retaining sandbox, permission, and evidence gates.
sources.risk: Example executors can be unsuitable for production without sandboxing and authorization.

sources.vendor_claim: Coze presents a natural-language Agent workflow that can decompose requirements, generate code, preview results, and deploy artifacts.
sources.current_model_signal: Coze is a multi-model platform; selectable foundation models remain separate from platform capability claims.
sources.anti_fomo_comparison: Anti-FOMO is stronger in traceability and fail-closed evidence; Coze emphasizes fast end-to-end creation and deployment.
sources.next_step: Improve proposal and artifact-diff UX without introducing one-click unreviewed deployment.
sources.risk: Automatic deployment or code execution exceeds the current authorization boundary.

sources.vendor_claim: Manus documents multi-step agent tasks, shared projects, file attachments, webhooks, and built-in or custom skills.
sources.current_model_signal: The observed official API v2 source does not promise one fixed foundation model, so model identity remains unknown.
sources.anti_fomo_comparison: Anti-FOMO has a stronger evidence-to-decision governance chain but a narrower external task and deliverable execution surface.
sources.next_step: Provide reviewable external-result return packets and skill metadata without automatically triggering external actions.
sources.risk: File, callback, and remote-task integrations require explicit identity, permission, and replay controls.
